subject: RosaHealth — DPA redline harmonization + export evidence checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@rosahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@rosahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T09:14:00Z
Subject: RosaHealth — DPA redline harmonization + export evidence checklist

Hi Marta / Rosa procurement team —

Thanks again for sending the initial DPA redlines. We reviewed the file and attached a consolidated mark-up (see RosaHealth_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf) that tries to harmonize your asks with Redwood standard language. Two parallel threads we need to resolve before legal can sign off:

1) SCCs / transfer mechanism: your team prefers referencing the client-side SCCs v2 bolt-in. We can accept SCCs as the transfer mechanism but need concrete language for fallback routing and a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) for any on-prem or VPC exceptions.

2) Export evidence & subprocessor list: procurement asked for a detailed evidence pack (export paths, KMS locations, subprocessor inventory). To avoid repeated back-and-forth, please confirm whether the following items will be sufficient:
  - current subprocessor list (CSV) with roles/regions
  - dataflow diagram that shows ingestion -> KV cache -> long-term storage
  - KMS key region(s) and provider names (for logs/metrics)
  - export evidence inventory (we attached a template: export-evidence-inventory.xlsx)

Operational nuance: RosaHealth requested a clause preventing cross-border routing for certain EU resident records. If you intend to lock routing at the application level we need the order form to call out hosting selection (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) so the runtime routing policy can be honored.

Attached: RosaHealth_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf (consolidated redline), export-evidence-inventory.xlsx (template).

Proposed next steps:
  - Your legal -> confirm SCCs preference (SCCs v2 with TIA vs bespoke transfer addendum)
  - Procurement -> confirm whether the export evidence template covers the team’s needs
  - Internal: if both answers are yes, Ben (legal) will prepare final compromise language for the MSA/Order Form tie-out and we’ll circulate for signature.

Can we aim to close this by EOD Friday (2027-01-02) so procurement can meet their vendor cutover? Happy to hop on a 30-minute sync if helpful.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Lead, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RosaHealth_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf (PDF, 42 pages), export-evidence-inventory.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

Subject: Re: RosaHealth — DPA redline harmonization + export evidence checklist

Jonas —

Appreciate the consolidated view. I’ve looped in our external counsel (Samuel) and procurement for the evidence questions. Quick responses:

- SCCs: we prefer referencing the EU SCCs v2 clause (our standard). We will consider a TIA for any non-standard hosting exceptions but need to be explicit about what triggers the TIA (e.g., dedicated on-prem with alternate KMS).

- Evidence pack: procurement confirms the template looks good, but they want items split by environment (prod/stage) and minimum timestamps for logs. Also: can you confirm you can provide "chain of custody" for exports (logs + transfer job IDs) for at least 90 days?

Operational ask: we raised the routing concern with our engineering team — they insist on explicit Order Form language that maps the chosen hosting profile to a region / routing guarantee. Without that, our security team won’t approve the product for PHI handling.

I attached RosaHealth’s redline for your DPA (RosaHealth_SCCs_comments.docx) with some alternate phrasing suggestions — mostly around liability waterfall and the definition of "process" vs "transfer".

Two questions for Redwood to confirm:
  1) Can Redwood provide a limited export-evidence snapshot (logs + KMS key id + transfer job id) for 90 days? If not, what retention period is realistic?
  2) On SCCs fallback: if Redwood pushes patches that change hosting behavior (e.g., a routing optimization), who signs the operational change notice and how is it recorded in contract (Order Form or Console SLA)?

We’ll wait for Ben’s suggested language and then route to our security team. If we can get on a call Thursday morning (your time) that would be helpful.

Thanks,

Marta Lopez
Head of Procurement & Privacy, RosaHealth

Attachments: RosaHealth_SCCs_comments.docx (Word, 6 pages)

Marta / team —

Thanks for the quick read. High-level position from Redwood legal with suggested draft language below. I also attached a short tracked-changes doc and called out a couple of tradeoffs.

1) SCCs + TIA approach (recommended compromise)
   - Insert language into the DPA: "The Parties agree that transfers from the EEA/UK shall be governed by the standard contractual clauses (EU Commission Decision 2021/914) as incorporated by reference. For hosting environments that materially alter the transfer pathway (including Dedicated private deployments or on-premise installations), the Parties shall execute a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) limited in scope to the affected dataflows."
   - Rationale: preserves client's desire for SCCs while giving Redwood an operational fallback to document exceptions per deployment.

2) Export evidence / retention
   - We can commit to a 90-day export log snapshot for transfer job IDs, KMS key id, and a per-transfer routing header. We want to reserve a longer-term retention add-on (12 months) as an optional paid service.
   - Insert into Order Form: a line item for "Export evidence retention: 90 days included; 12 months optional (paid)."

3) Routing / operational-change notice
   - Proposed: changes that materially affect routing will be recorded in Console change logs and require an operational-change notice to the customer. Contractually, the Order Form will state that routing guarantees apply only when the customer selects "Dedicated" or "Private" hosting profiles. Hosted plans will have best-effort routing and the routing SLA defined in the hosting addendum.

4) Liability / waterfall (client redline concern)
   - We propose a moderate adjustment to your waterfall: keep a customer-friendly cap for export incidents tied to fees but preserve Redwood’s carve-outs for gross negligence or willful misconduct. Language snippet included in attached doc.

Attachments: RosaHealth_SCCs_comments.docx (our tracked copy)

If that sounds acceptable I’ll produce a tracked DPA + a one-pager TIA template you can sign to expedite procurement. Otherwise please flag specific clauses and we’ll iterate.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
